references.text: The preceding verse deals with unclean earthenware vessels and how they become unclean when something unclean falls into them, providing context for verse 34 regarding food and drink in such vessels.
It concerns seed grain that becomes unclean when water comes upon it and is subsequently touched by a carcass, elaborating on the principle that water can transmit uncleanness to food.
Earthenware vessels touched by a man with a discharge must be broken, and wooden vessels shall be rinsed with water. Parallel legislation concerning uncleanness in vessels.
Any open vessel without a lid becomes unclean. It elaborates on the rules regarding how vessels can become unclean.
It addresses the consequences of uncleanness and the desecration of the sanctuary, illustrating the seriousness of the laws of purity.
Jesus teaches that it is not what enters the mouth that makes a person unclean, but what comes out of the mouth. A New Testament reinterpretation of the purity laws in Leviticus.
Jesus declares all food clean and teaches that uncleanness comes from the heart, not from external things. It represents a fulfillment and reinterpretation of the Old Testament purity laws.
